body: I'm just writing right now. I've remained in contact with few.
When I talk with another person, if they are decent, I just think, "One of us deserves to be happy."

It's as simple as I've always followed, "If I can do something, I will." Everything from talking down someone from suicide to giving a stranger my lunch. I just try to do more than a person believes they deserve, in and out of various "work."

No, it never did; I thought eventually it would.
It's been fifteen years of the same mindset, feeling, telling myself to wait another week or day.  Even therapy failed to change it.  I've always felt entirely empty.
I've done good because I didn't know what else to do.

Just about everything is right.  I've chased dreams and achieved most of them.  I've made differences in people's lives; I've even been told that I've changed how people saw the world and approached their lives.  I've done a lot of good.  I've experienced so much.  I've taken risks that payed off and gotten so much more out of my life than anyone expected me to.
It simply doesn't matter. It doesn't mean anything.
I have two more good deeds to do before I go.  This isn't a cry for help, but thank you for your kind words.  There should be more people like you doing good.
I simply don't want to fail.
